archetype.name: Game Manager (mobile backup)
archetype.definition: A spot starter who keeps the Ravens on schedule with screens, checkdowns and quick outs, protects the ball and adds some legs, but rarely pushes it downfield and takes too many sacks to lift the offense.

report.headline: A competent fill-in whose sacks and scattershot accuracy cap the offense's ceiling.
report.take:
Huntley is what he has been for six seasons: a short-area distributor who keeps the offense functional when Lamar Jackson is out. His intended air yards sit at 6.69 and he throws 2.25 yards short of the sticks on average. He works behind the line and inside ten yards, and he almost never throws a pick: his 0.9% interception rate ranks 10th of 47. In his three starts (Weeks 5-7) the offense held up at 0.107 EPA per dropback and 221.3 passing yards a game. That is roughly league-average quarterbacking, from a player Baltimore only needs to be average.

The season line looks worse than his play because of the Week 8 cameo in Buffalo. He took 20% of the snaps, went 2-of-4 for zero yards, was sacked once, lost a fumble and posted -9.3 passing EPA. That one appearance accounts for most of the damage in his trailing-by-9-plus split, and it pulls his last-three-games window negative. Judged on his starts alone, the passing value was real, and it came from an odd place. His 22 intermediate throws produced 0.61 EPA each, while his short game, the core of his style, was slightly negative at -0.065.

The soft spots are structural. He takes sacks: a 9.1% sack rate ranks 39th of 47, and 41.7% of his pressures become sacks, 36th of 38. His career pressure-to-sack rates have sat between 0.357 and 0.8, so this is not new. Holding the ball to extend plays isn't paying off either: nine scrambles produced zero first downs. His accuracy has also slipped. His bad-throw rate rose from 9.7% in Week 5 to 19.4% and then 23.5%. Last year's 12.9 CPOE and 77.6% completion rate were a four-game mirage, and this year's 2.94 CPOE is much closer to his career norm.

Now the situation has turned. Jackson is headed for thumb surgery and injured reserve with a mid-December target, which made Huntley QB1. But Huntley sprained a toe, and his coach says he probably won't play Thursday. The question is no longer how good he is as a starter. It is how many of the remaining Jackson-less starts he will be healthy enough to take.

strengths.title: Ball security in a low-risk offense
strengths.body: He has one interception in 110 attempts, and his interception rate is 1.4 points under the league average. That follows from a quick-game diet that keeps throws short and away from traffic. He also threw no picks in 2023 or 2025, so this is a durable trait that will hold.

strengths.title: Intermediate throws carried the passing value
strengths.body: His 22 throws at 10-19 air yards added 0.61 EPA each, the biggest chunk of his passing value, even though only 54.5% were completed. Throws to the left side were similarly productive. Twenty-two attempts is a hint rather than a law, and the -6.5 CPOE there says some of it was catch-and-run luck. Expect it to cool, though not to flip negative.

strengths.title: Offense functioned in his starts
strengths.body: Across Weeks 5-7 the passing game ran at 0.107 EPA per dropback, with 17.5 PPR points a game. That is a starter-caliber floor for a backup. Bateman and Cuevas were especially efficient targets for him, which suggests the timing throws to the perimeter and the tight end work.

concerns.title: Sacks swallow the drive value
concerns.body: Nearly half his pressures end in sacks, and the scrambles that come from holding the ball have produced no first downs. That is why his dropback EPA total is negative while his passing EPA is positive. It has been his profile throughout his career, not a slump, and a line already ranked 25th in hits allowed only makes it worse.

concerns.title: Accuracy has drifted the wrong way
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate ranks 30th of 38, and it climbed in each start. His CPOE fell from 6.4 against Atlanta to negative in the next two games, and throws over the middle have been poor (-17.1 CPOE). Last season's pinpoint accuracy looks like small-sample noise, and this level is closer to his career baseline.

concerns.title: No downfield dimension, and Andrews misfiring
concerns.body: He completed one of seven deep attempts, so defenses can sit on the short game. His throws to Mark Andrews have been a big drain, which takes a reliable middle-of-field outlet off the table.

trend.note: Passing EPA stayed positive in all three starts, but his accuracy markers slid each week. The Buffalo cameo then ended with a fumble and a toe sprain that now threatens his short-term availability.

nextGame.headline: Likely sidelined; if he plays, Jacksonville's short-area defense smothers his game.
nextGame.body:
Jacksonville is about the worst stylistic draw for him. It ranks 3rd in defensive EPA and 4th against the pass, and it is the league's best defense on short throws (-0.322 EPA). That is exactly where he lives. Its weakness is deep passing, where it ranks 29th, but Huntley has barely attacked that area. The Jaguars also rank 2nd against the run, which leaves Baltimore leaning on the pass on a Thursday with four days' rest. The Book has the Ravens as 8.5-point home underdogs with a 42.5 total, a game script that projects trailing and obvious passing downs. Those are the situations where his sack habit hurts most.

Availability is the story. Coach Jesse Minter said Huntley probably won't play, and the alternative, Joe Fagnano, is himself limited with an ankle. Up front, guard Olaivavega Ioane is out, and starters Roger Rosengarten and John Simpson are questionable. Any of those absences adds to the pressure problem. On the other side, Jacksonville is down two safeties, Antonio Johnson and Eric Murray (out for the season), and DT DaVon Hamilton. Edge Travon Walker (ribs) and CB Jarrian Jones are questionable. A thinner back end is the one opening for intermediate and deep shots to Flowers and Bateman.

keyMatchups.title: Quick game versus the league's best short defense
keyMatchups.body: His short throws were already slightly negative, and Jacksonville allows the least on those throws of any defense. Without a willingness to push the ball, drives will stall. This is a matchup to fade, not a sample-size quirk.

keyMatchups.title: Flowers against a leaky WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Jacksonville gives up 0.61 EPA a target to opposing WR1s, 29th in the league, though it has held them under their usual fantasy output. Flowers has been his most-targeted receiver and is efficient, so the depleted safety group could open intermediate windows for him.

keyMatchups.title: Patchwork line, short week
keyMatchups.body: With Ioane out and two other 100%-snap starters questionable, the protection that already ranks 25th in hits allowed could get worse. For a quarterback who turns pressure into sacks this often, that is the biggest threat to any passing output.

nextGame.watch: Whether Huntley is active at all, and if Fagnano starts, whether the Ravens' plan shifts even further to the short game Jacksonville shuts down.

restOfSeason.body:
The ceiling is set by the calendar and his toe. Jackson's expected return is mid-December, so Huntley's value rests on however many starts he can make between his recovery and that date, and Minter's comment about a long-term look adds real doubt. When he does start, expect what Weeks 5-7 showed: an efficient-enough, low-turnover passing game around 6.5-7 yards an attempt. Expect few touchdowns, two to four sacks a game, and a little rushing.

The interception avoidance should hold, since it is a career trait. The intermediate efficiency should cool toward neutral, and the accuracy decline is more likely his true level than a dip. The projections below are for games he starts; as a backup his weekly output is close to zero.
swingFactors: How long the toe sprain lingers
Health of Ioane, Rosengarten and Simpson up front

confidence.note: Three starts, an injury of uncertain length and a starter returning in December.
